CLOSED 2026-11-24. pkix-dane-resolver released at 0.2.0 (was a 0.1.0 namespace stub), plus the new sibling crate pkix-dnssec-anchor 0.1.0.

## Shipped

pkix-dane-resolver: AsyncTlsaResolver trait (async-trait, batch_resolve joins concurrently, impl for Arc<T>), HickoryTlsaResolver, NoAsyncTlsaResolver, UpstreamConfig + upstream_from_environment, ResolverError. 22 tests; fmt / clippy / rustdoc -D warnings / typos clean.

pkix-dnssec-anchor: RootAnchor, CURRENT and ALL, new() plus with_* builders, is_valid_at / is_withdrawn / is_key_signing_key, and gen.sh + gen.py which verify IANA's detached PKCS#7 signature before generating. 18 tests.

## Open shape decisions from this bead, resolved

- "Sync wrapper over async hickory: spawn_blocking + ad-hoc runtime, or expose async only?" -> ASYNC ONLY. Mark's principle: hiding a thread inside a sync API is what async exists to avoid. block_on panics from inside a Tokio runtime; the reqwest::blocking background-thread shape works but hides an executor behind a blocking-looking signature. The sync path takes records as data instead, which works because pkix-dane's matchers are pure over (certificate, TlsaResponse).
- "Cache strategy: in-memory only, or admit on-disk cache via trait?" -> NEITHER SHIPS. The trait admits a wrapper (&self receivers, Clone + PartialEq response) per non-negotiable #6, which requires the workspace to admit caches rather than build them. Hickory's own response cache still applies underneath. Filed as follow-up.
- "Hickory feature set: minimum needed for DNSSEC." -> system-config, tokio, dnssec-ring. Nothing else.

## Acceptance

[x] Resolver trait + default hickory-backed impl
[x] DNSSEC validation. Verified end-to-end, not merely wired: a signed zone (good.dane.huque.com) returns Secure with records, an unsigned one does not. That pair is the test that distinguishes real validation from a resolver that reports everything secure.
[ ] In-memory TLSA cache with TTL respect -- NOT DONE, deliberately. See above.
[x] System resolv.conf as default upstream, with the PKIX_DANE_RESOLVER override decided in PKIX-j32w.5
[x] Smoke test against a public DANE-deployed name
[x] ResolverError satisfies non-negotiable #6

## Two findings worth carrying forward

1. systemd-resolved's stub listener on 127.0.0.53 -- what /etc/resolv.conf points at on most modern Linux desktops -- validates internally and STRIPS DNSSEC records from client answers. A validating client behind it sees every answer as unvalidatable. This is not hypothetical: it is why the live tests appeared to fail here. It is exactly the upstream-mangling case the env override exists for, and it means "DANE works out of the box on Linux" is false for the default system resolver. Worth stating prominently in any consumer-facing documentation.

2. dns.google publishes NO TLSA records. It was the obvious-looking smoke-test target and is useless for the purpose. good.dane.huque.com (Shumon Huque's DANE test domain) is signed and publishes usage 3 / selector 1 / matching 1 at port 443.

Also worth recording: an earlier draft of the live tests reported the DNSSEC-stripping failure as "likely no network", which masked a real signal as an environmental skip. Fixed; the skip logic now classifies the error and says which case it is. That class of mistake -- a skip message that guesses -- is worth watching for elsewhere.

## Follow-ons filed

- TTL cache for pkix-dane-resolver
- Signed negative answers should report Secure so TlsaResponse::is_authenticated_denial can see them; currently Indeterminate, which is fail-closed but less informative. Needs the SOA's proof off hickory's negative-response error.
- PKIX-4bxy: the IANA KSK-roll obligation on pkix-dnssec-anchor
- PKIX-rgc6: SMTP-DANE, which needs the DNSSEC-validated MX lookup this crate does not do
